newsitem.title: USA: American Radio says Q1 unsustainable.
newsitem.headline: American Radio says Q1 unsustainable.

text.p: American Radio Systems Corp Chief Executive Steve Dodge said the company's strong first quarter results are unsustainable over the entire year.

"I think the first quarter numbers, and I'm trying to urge some caution here, are extremely strong and I don't think over the course of the full year sustainable," Dodge told analysts on the conference call.

"The second quarter will not be as good a growth quarter for us as the third and fourth quarters will be. And then for the year, we still remain comfortable with the analysts' estimates of $150 million or so of proforma cash flow."
Dodge said that the proforma cash flow figures for the year could perhaps be "a little bit better" than $150 million.
Revenue growth on a same-station basis, which compares stations owned or operated during the period with the their previous results, will continue to grow at a strong rate.
"We're quite comfortable averaging growth rates in the high-teens to low 20s over the next three to four years on a same-station basis from our existing group of radio stations," he said.
While same-station cash flow will grow at a rate of around 20 percent, revenues from those stations will continue strong but not at the same pace as the first quarter, he said.
American Radio reported late Tuesday that same-station revenues grew 17.3 percent in the first quarter from the previous first quarter while net revenues grew by 129.7 percent.
"For you to expect us or any other radio company to produce mid- to high-teens revenue growth is very unrealistic. I think, you know, 11 to 12 percent range is more realistic," he said.
Dodge said same-station revenues will grow because the company has 18 "highly-underdeveloped" stations which overall contributed zero cash flow last year.
Over the next four to five years they will contribute cash flows of around $2 million each and have operating margins of around 45 percent, he said.

In addition, 16 or 17 stations at "middle stage development" will contribute the greatest growth in the near-term, he said. Their operating margins will grow to the mid-40 percent range in a year or two from around 35 percent now, he said.
